name: IL-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+20 partisan lean makes a Democratic win extremely unlikely
Incumbent Mary Miller holds a large financial advantage over Jennifer Todd
Prediction markets price Miller at roughly 96% to win
No public general-election polling is available for this race
model.rationale: The R+20 district fundamentals, Miller's roughly $810,000 cash advantage over Todd's $34,000, and prediction markets pricing her near 96% all point the same direction, so the forecast stays close to the baseline at about a 19-point Republican margin. No polls or expert ratings exist to justify moving away from that picture.
model.watch: Any credible general-election polling showing Miller underperforming her district's lean, or significant outside spending against her, would be the first sign the race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mary Miller, the incumbent Republican, is seeking another term in a heavily Republican southern Illinois district with a partisan lean of about R+20. Jennifer Todd, the Democratic challenger, has raised about $113,000 and had roughly $34,000 on hand, while Miller has raised about $1.3 million and holds more than $810,000 in cash. Outside spending on both sides has been minimal.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and campaign finance. Prediction markets give Miller about a 96% chance of winning. The district's strong Republican tilt and the incumbent's financial edge make an upset very unlikely, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
